title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 1: The sound, and where it came from
description: How Japan built its own fusion scene, the four traits that define it, and the pioneers who opened the door.

title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 2: Sadao Watanabe, the elder statesman
description: The saxophonist who connected Japanese jazz to the world, from bossa nova and Africa to sunny Los Angeles fusion.

title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 3: Masayoshi Takanaka, the guitar that sings
description: Takanaka's vocal, tropical guitar, his Latin obsession, and the showman behind it.

title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 4: Casiopea, the precision machine
description: Casiopea's ensemble playing: unison lines, slap bass, busy drums and synthesizers, and why fans see them as the heart of the scene.

title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 5: T-Square, the anthem makers
description: T-Square's wind-synth lead, Masahiro Andoh's anthems, and how their music reached TV, school bands and video games.

title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 6: Kazumi Watanabe, the virtuoso
description: The guitarist who broke the rules of the style: harder, darker, more technical, and closest to American fusion.

title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 7: Spin-offs: when band members go solo
description: What happens when the players behind Casiopea and T-Square step out on their own, and what that reveals about each musician.

title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 8: Legacy: city pop, the internet and the heirs
description: How fusion fed city pop, how the internet rediscovered it decades later, and who carries the sound today.
